items.title: Howard Alden interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: I know that with the great drummers that I’ve gotten to play with, it’s usually just settled into a great groove, whether it’s Jake or Al Harewood or any of those guys.

ctx.x: Like rushing without speeding up I guess.

I don’t think that really exists though, the more I think about it. If you’re playing on top of the beat, you’re just slightly rushing, that’s all. And the other guys trying not to rush maybe hold him back, maybe not. I know that with the great drummers that I’ve gotten to play with, it’s usually just settled into a great groove, whether it’s Jake or Al Harewood or any of those guys. Yeah, I don’t think it really exists. Ask Jake about it. You’ll get a good answer from him.
Okay, I will. Let’s suppose, just to wrap up here, let’s suppose you could put a dream band together to do a six month tour of the world.
